|date=30 July 2025 |language=en}} ==Summary== ===Background=== Wolverhampton was created in 1974 as a [[metropolitan borough]], gaining [[City status in the United Kingdom|city status]] in 2000. Since its creation, the council has either been controlled by [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] or under [[no overall control]].{{cite news |title=BBC News - Election 2011 - England council elections - Wolverhampton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/special/election2011/council/html/cw.stm |access-date=14 January 2026 |work=BBC News}} No party held a majority between [[1987 Wolverhampton Metropolitan Borough Council election|1987]] and [[1988 Wolverhampton Metropolitan Borough Council election|1988]], between [[1992 Wolverhampton Metropolitan Borough Council election|1992]] and [[1994 Wolverhampton Metropolitan Borough Council election|1994]], and between [[2008 Wolverhampton City Council election|2008]] and [[2011 Wolverhampton City Council election|2011]].{{cite web |title=Wolverhampton City Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=https://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Wolverhampton-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=14 January 2026}} Labour have held a majority for the previous 15 years, increasing their majority by 1 in [[2024 City of Wolverhampton Council election|2024]] through gaining a seat from the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]].{{cite news |title=Tories lose control of Dudley council after three years |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c2qvln91xrqo |access-date=14 January 2026 |work=BBC News |date=3 May 2024}} The [[2023 City of Wolverhampton Council election|2023 election]] took place on a new set of ward boundaries.[https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/967/made The Wolverhampton (Electoral Changes) Order 2022]. As such, these elections will be for the councillors elected with the second-highest number of votes.
